plan.note: Arrived early? Here's a suggested plan for the day, with more ideas below.

route.title: Harbour, the Peak & TST (full day)
steps: Ding ding tram west from Causeway Bay: Admiralty for Dim Sum Library (about 15 min) or Sheung Wan for Lin Heung Lau (about 30 min). Tap Visa/Mastercard or Octopus
Dim sum lunch on the way, e.g. Maxim's Palace at City Hall (no booking, go before noon)
Peak Tram up from Garden Road (10 min walk or a short taxi). HK$82 one way / HK$116 return. Buy e-tickets at thepeak.com.hk to skip the ticket queue
At the Peak: egg tart gelato at Messina, or milk tea at Men Wah Bing Teng
Walk the flat Peak Circle Walk (about 3.5 km / 2 miles). Lugard Road Lookout has the best view
Back down, then the Star Ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui
K11 Musea or the HK Museum of Art, then the TST Promenade for the 8pm Symphony of Lights

tips.title: Survival kit
items: 💳 Tap Visa or Mastercard on the MTR, buses, trams and in most shops.
💵 Carry HK$300–500 cash. Local spots and minibuses are often cash only.
🐙 Octopus card for everywhere else. On iPhone, get the "Octopus for Tourists" app and pay with Apple Pay. Or buy a card at any MTR station.
🚕 Taxi? Tap "Show the driver" on any place and hand over your phone.
🛗 Escalators: stand on the right, walk on the left.
🧭 Citymapper is the best app for getting around.

tips.title: Did you know?
items: 🇬🇧 A British colony until 1997, now part of China under "one country, two systems". It keeps its own currency, passport and laws, and cars still drive on the left.
🏙️ More skyscrapers than any other city on Earth, yet about 40% of the land is country park.
🛗 The Central–Mid-Levels escalator is the world's longest outdoor covered escalator, about 800 m uphill.
🚋 The ding ding trams are the world's largest double-decker tram fleet, running since 1904.

add.name: Afternoon tea at The Peninsula
add.intro: Tiered scones, finger sandwiches and a string quartet in the gilded lobby of Hong Kong's oldest hotel, opened in 1928. It's a quintessential colonial-era Hong Kong ritual.
add.funFact: During the Second World War, the British governor surrendered Hong Kong to Japan at The Peninsula on Christmas Day 1941, in a room on the hotel's third floor.
add.tips: Go mid-afternoon on a weekday and expect a queue. Check The Peninsula's website for current booking rules. Afterwards, walk five minutes to the Tsim Sha Tsui promenade for the skyline, and stay for the 8pm Symphony of Lights.
add.getting: From the Park Lane: MTR from Causeway Bay to Tsim Sha Tsui (about 20 min), or take the Star Ferry from Wan Chai.
add.mapsQuery: The Lobby The Peninsula Hong Kong

add.name: Mott 32
add.intro: A glamorous, moody basement restaurant in an old bank building, and one of Hong Kong's most famous Chinese restaurants.
order: Applewood-roasted Peking duck (book it when you reserve)
add.reviews: Loved for the room and the duck; it's pricey, and the duck's second course costs extra.
add.tips: Book ahead on SevenRooms and pre-order the duck. Lunch is 11:30–2:30 and dinner 5:30 till late.
add.addressEn: Basement, Standard Chartered Bank Building, 4-4A Des Voeux Road Central
add.addressZh: 中環德輔道中4-4A號渣打銀行大廈地庫
add.mapsQuery: Mott 32 Standard Chartered Bank Building Central

add.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
add.intro: A calm, air-conditioned stop with Chinese painting, calligraphy and Hong Kong art, plus harbour views from the galleries. Easy to pair with a walk along the TST Promenade.
add.getting: MTR from Causeway Bay to Tsim Sha Tsui (change at Admiralty or Tsim Sha Tsui via Tsuen Wan line), about 20-25 min, then a 10-min walk. Or Star Ferry from Central, about 10 min.
add.tips: Closed on Thursdays (so not Thu 19 Nov). The permanent collection is free, and special exhibitions are ticketed. Time it so you walk out onto the Promenade for sunset and the 8pm Symphony of Lights.
add.addressEn: 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon
add.addressZh: 香港九龍尖沙咀梳士巴利道10號

add.name: Big Buddha & Ngong Ping 360 cable car
add.zh: 天壇大佛、寶蓮禪寺及昂坪360
add.intro: Ride a 25-minute cable car over the bay and mountains to a 34-metre bronze Buddha and a lively working monastery. It is Hong Kong's classic half-day escape from the city.
add.getting: MTR to Tung Chung (Causeway Bay to Tung Chung about 45 min, change at Central/Hong Kong or Lai King), then Ngong Ping 360 cable car about 25 min. Or bus 23 from Tung Chung.
add.tips: Book cable car online in advance and go early on a weekday to avoid long queues; check the cable car is running that day.
add.hours: Cable car: weekdays 10:00-18:00, weekends and public holidays 09:00-18:30; service can pause for wind or maintenance
add.addressEn: Ngong Ping, Lantau Island (Ngong Ping 360 terminal: Tung Chung)
add.addressZh: 香港大嶼山昂坪寶蓮禪寺(天壇大佛)
add.priceNote: Standard cabin return roughly HK$235 weekdays, more at weekends (sources vary; check official site); Buddha grounds free, 268 steps to climb
add.funFact: The Big Buddha is 34 m tall and was the world's largest seated outdoor bronze Buddha when it was finished in 1993. There are 268 steps to the top.

add.name: Tai O Fishing Village
add.intro: A traditional fishing village with stilt houses over the tidal creek, small boat rides, salted fish stalls and local snacks. It shows an older Hong Kong that few visitors see.
add.getting: From Ngong Ping/Big Buddha take bus 21 (about 30 min); from Tung Chung bus 11 (about 40 min). From Causeway Bay allow about 1.5 to 2 hours.
add.tips: Pair with the Big Buddha and head to Tai O in the afternoon; go on a weekday as weekends get crowded.
add.hours: Village open all day; most shops and stalls roughly 10:00-18:00
add.addressEn: Tai O, Lantau Island
add.priceNote: Free to wander; snacks and boat ride are a few HK$ to about HK$30
add.funFact: Tai O's stilt houses (pang uk) belong to the Tanka boat people, who have fished these waters for centuries. Look for the shrimp paste and salted fish drying in the sun.

add.name: Cheung Chau Island
add.intro: A car-free island with a seafront promenade, beaches, temples and street snacks like fish balls and mango mochi. Famous for the Cheung Chau Bun Festival, when people once climbed towers of buns, a tradition that continues in spring.
add.getting: MTR to Central, walk to Central Pier 5; Fast ferry about 35 min, ordinary ferry about 55 min. Causeway Bay to Central about 10 min by MTR.
add.tips: Take the fast ferry out and the slow ferry back for the harbour view; check ferry timetable on the operator site.
add.hours: Ferries run roughly 06:00 to after midnight; shops and cafes mostly open daytime to evening
add.addressEn: Cheung Chau Ferry Pier, San Hing Praya Street, Cheung Chau
add.addressZh: 香港長洲新興海傍街長洲碼頭
add.priceNote: Ferry about HK$17 to HK$37 one way depending on class and day; snacks HK$10 to HK$40
add.funFact: There are no cars on Cheung Chau, just bikes and tiny village trucks. At the spring Bun Festival, climbers race up a 14 m tower covered in buns.

add.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
add.intro: A compact Disney park with Frozen, Marvel and Toy Story lands and fewer crowds than other Disney parks. Fun for a break from city sightseeing.
add.getting: MTR to Sunny Bay, change to the Disneyland Resort line to Disneyland Resort station. About 50 min from Causeway Bay.
add.tips: Buy tickets online and arrive before opening; weekdays are far quieter; ride Premier Access for popular rides if you have limited time.
add.addressEn: Lantau Island, Hong Kong
add.addressZh: 香港大嶼山香港迪士尼樂園
add.priceNote: One-day ticket about HK$639 to HK$879 depending on the date tier (sources vary)

add.name: Ocean Park (giant pandas)
add.intro: Hong Kong's homegrown marine park with roller coasters, a cable car and giant pandas, including twin cubs born in 2024. Good for classmates who like rides and animals, and it is close to the school side of the island.
add.getting: MTR from Causeway Bay to Admiralty, change to the South Island line to Ocean Park station, about 20-25 min.
add.tips: See the pandas first thing, when they're most active (their area closes earlier than the park). Then take the South Island line two stops to Lei Tung for a seafood dinner in Ap Lei Chau.
add.hours: Roughly 10:00-18:30 or 19:30 daily; Giant Panda Adventure has shorter hours that changed on 3 November 2026, so check the daily schedule
add.addressEn: Ocean Park, Nam Long Shan Road, Aberdeen
add.addressZh: 香港仔南朗山道香港海洋公園
add.priceNote: Adult about HK$538, child about HK$269 (third-party sources); Water World is a separate ticket
facts: Seafood dinner in Ap Lei Chau

add.name: Ap Lei Chau seafood (pick it, they cook it)
add.zh: 鴨脷洲街市及熟食中心
add.intro: Pick live fish, prawns and crab from the market downstairs, then have the stalls upstairs cook it for you. Stalls like Yiu Kee, Chan Sun Kee and Chu Kee are well known for this. Good for an after Ocean Park dinner.
add.getting: MTR South Island line to Lei Tung station (exits A1/A2), a few stops from Ocean Park; from Causeway Bay via Admiralty about 30 min.
add.tips: Buy live seafood at the market downstairs, then have a stall upstairs (Yiu Kee, Chan Sun Kee or Chu Kee) cook it. Agree the price per catty and the cooking fee first, bring cash, and book a table on busy evenings. It's perfect after Ocean Park.
add.hours: Market from morning; cooked food stalls generally lunch and dinner (hours vary by stall)
add.addressEn: Ap Lei Chau Municipal Services Building, 8 Hung Shing Street, Ap Lei Chau
add.addressZh: 香港鴨脷洲洪聖街8號鴨脷洲市政大廈

add.name: Men Wah Bing Teng (Peak Galleria)
add.intro: A Hong Kong-style tea restaurant with milk tea, pineapple buns, egg tarts and baked pork chop rice, with a branch at the Peak Galleria. A cosy local meal after the Peak views.
add.getting: Peak Tram from Garden Road (Central) about 10 min, or bus 15 from Central Pier; the Galleria is by the Peak Tower. Causeway Bay to Central about 10 min.
add.tips: Egg tarts sell out soon after coming out of the oven, so order early.
add.hours: Hang Lung Malls lists Mon-Thu 10:00-21:30, Fri-Sun and holidays 10:00-22:00 (OpenRice shows 10:00-20:30; confirm)
add.addressEn: Shop 205, 2/F, Peak Galleria, 118 Peak Road, The Peak
add.addressZh: 香港山頂山頂道118號山頂廣場2樓205號舖

add.name: Messina (the Peak) · egg tart gelato
add.intro: Australian gelato with a Hong Kong exclusive egg tart flavour, egg custard gelato layered with caramelised puff pastry. A good cool-down treat on the Peak.
add.getting: Peak Tram from Garden Road (Central) about 10 min, or bus 15; the Galleria is next to the Peak Tower.
add.tips: Get the Hong Kong-only egg tart flavour, which is custard gelato with caramelised puff pastry. Check opening hours before you go.
add.hours: Not confirmed for this branch (an Instagram post gives Mon-Thu 12:00-22:00, Fri-Sun 12:00-23:00, possibly other outlet); check before going
add.addressEn: Shop G08, G/F, Peak Galleria, 118 Peak Road, The Peak
add.addressZh: 香港山頂山頂道118號山頂廣場地下G08號舖

add.name: Ladies' Market (Tung Choi Street)
add.intro: A kilometre of street stalls under the Mong Kok neon: T-shirts, phone cases, bags, souvenirs and snacks. It's loud, crowded and a great slice of Kowloon street life.
add.tips: Haggle with a smile and start at about half the asking price. Go after dark (stalls run from about noon to 11pm), and then walk the neon streets around Sai Yeung Choi Street. Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket.
add.getting: MTR to Mong Kok (Exit D3), about 25 min from Causeway Bay. Or a taxi, 20–30 min via the Cross-Harbour Tunnel.
add.addressEn: Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok, Kowloon
add.addressZh: 九龍旺角通菜街（女人街）
add.mapsQuery: Ladies' Market Tung Choi Street Mong Kok Hong Kong

add.name: Hong Kong Palace Museum
add.intro: Treasures from Beijing's Forbidden City, including imperial paintings, porcelain and jade, in a striking new building on the West Kowloon waterfront. Pair it with M+ next door and a harbour walk.
add.tips: Book a timed ticket online, especially for special exhibitions. Allow 2 hours. M+ and the West Kowloon Art Park are a few minutes' walk away for sunset skyline views.
add.getting: Ferry: the WestK Ferry from Central Pier 9 to West Kowloon takes about 8 min (HK$20, every 15–30 min). It was licensed on a trial until 9 Nov 2026, so check it's still running. Otherwise MTR to Kowloon or Austin station and a 10-min walk, or a 15-min taxi from Central.
add.addressEn: 8 Museum Drive, West Kowloon Cultural District
add.addressZh: 九龍西九文化區博物館道8號香港故宮文化博物館

add.name: T'ang Court
add.intro: One of the world's few three-Michelin-star Cantonese restaurants, in a elegant dining room at the Langham. The place for a celebratory dinner or a polished dim sum lunch.
order: Stir-fried lobster with three kinds of onions
add.tips: Book well ahead (own bookings; call). Smart casual; no shorts at dinner. Dim sum at lunch is the easier, cheaper way in.
add.addressEn: 1/F & 2/F, The Langham Hong Kong, 8 Peking Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Yat Tung Heen (Eaton HK)
add.intro: A one-star Cantonese restaurant that has been serving refined traditional food since 1990, with strong dim sum and barbecued meats at far friendlier prices than the Peninsula-style hotels. Good for groups at a round table.
order: Dim sum selection (turnip pudding, shrimp dumplings)
add.tips: Call to book (own bookings), especially weekends and for 6+. Dim sum served at lunch and weekends from 10:00.
add.addressEn: B2/F, Eaton HK, 380 Nathan Road, Jordan, Kowloon

add.name: Sun Tung Lok
add.intro: A veteran Hong Kong banquet name, open since 1969, known for premium dried seafood and a show-stopping suckling pig. Comfortable for big groups and business-style dinners.
order: Crispy roast suckling pig stuffed with minced shrimp
Steamed seafood dumplings with bamboo pith
add.tips: Call to book (own bookings). Set menus are the easy choice for groups. Inside Mira Place mall, 4/F.
add.addressEn: Shop 401, 4/F, FoodLoft, Mira Place One, 132 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Tai Ping Koon (Granville Road)
add.intro: Hong Kong's oldest Western-style restaurant, a family business dating to 1860 and inventor of the 'Swiss' chicken wing. A nostalgic, uniquely Hong Kong meal that locals still love.
add.tips: Walk-ins fine; busy at peak meal times and weekends. Order the souffle when you sit down. Food is nostalgic rather than cutting-edge; some reviewers rate it mixed.
add.addressEn: G/F, 40 Granville Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Sushi Wadatsumi (K11 Musea)
add.intro: An intimate counter serving Edomae-style omakase from a one-star Tokyo-trained team. The lunch omakase is the sweet spot for a first taste of top-tier sushi.
add.tips: Reservations essential, very few seats (best for 2-6). Service charge extra. Prices from listings, may have changed.
add.addressEn: Shop 607, 6/F, K11 Musea, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Konjiki Hototogisu (H Zentre)
add.intro: Outpost of a Michelin-starred Tokyo ramen shop, famous for a delicate clam-and-pork broth. A quick, affordable Japanese stop near the harbour.
add.tips: Walk-in only; queues at peak times. Reviews mixed on noodle portion size. Michelin status of the HK branch not confirmed (Tokyo shop's stars are cited).
add.addressEn: G/F, H Zentre, 15 Middle Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Hancham Korean Meathouse (Prat Avenue)
add.intro: A modern Korean meathouse specialising in dry-aged cuts, with staff who grill at the table. Fun and social for groups. Recommended by Time Out HK.
add.tips: Book via Resy/OpenRice for groups. Lunch sets are good value. Coordinates and Chinese address approximate; phone not confirmed (sources conflict).
add.addressEn: 1/F, Winfield Commercial Building, 6-8A Prat Avenue, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Carna by Dario Cecchini
add.intro: Tuscan butcher Dario Cecchini's first Asian restaurant, with harbour views and charcoal-grilled cuts. A great splurge steak dinner for a group. Listed in the Michelin Guide and SCMP 100 Top Tables.
add.tips: Book on SevenRooms. Dinner nightly; weekend lunch. Weekday lunch not served. Michelin Guide listing (no star/Bib).
add.addressEn: 39/F, Mondrian Hong Kong, 8A Hart Avenue, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Chesa
add.intro: A cosy Alpine-chalet dining room with Swiss comfort food, renovated with a new menu in 2026. Fondue is a fun shared meal for a group.
order: Cheese fondue (mushroom and black truffle option)
add.tips: Book directly with the hotel. No windows, chalet look. Michelin 'Inspectors Favorite' (not starred).
add.addressEn: 1/F, The Peninsula Hong Kong, 22 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Yè Shanghai (K11 Musea)
add.intro: Art Deco, 1930s Shanghai-style dining room over two floors with harbour views. A friendly way to try Shanghainese classics and dim sum with a group.
add.tips: Call to book (own bookings); reserve a day ahead. Mall location, easy for a group.
add.addressEn: Shop 702, 7/F, K11 Musea, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Ho Ho Chak
add.intro: A new 2026 Bib Gourmand run by three brothers who wholesale seafood, so the ingredients are strong. A fine place to try Chiu Chow cooking.
order: Steamed pork patty with mud crab and roe
Fried oyster omelette (or dried radish omelette)
Chiu Chow-style sweet and sour noodles
add.tips: Reserve directly. 9th-floor of a building (lift to 9/F). Chinese name per OpenRice; confirm at booking.
add.addressEn: 9/F, Nathan Hill, 38 Hillwood Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Thai Pai Dong (Jordan)
add.intro: A lively little Thai spot loved for its wagyu boat noodles and punchy street dishes. Michelin recommends expecting a queue.
add.tips: Small, no bookings via Michelin (contact directly); queues at peak. Coordinates approximate. Michelin award tier: listed as Bib Gourmand on Michelin's TST page, not shown on the restaurant page.
add.addressEn: G/F, 24 Man Yuen Street, Jordan, Kowloon

add.name: Mak Man Kee Noodle Shop
add.intro: A no-frills noodle shop of about 60 years, famous for thin-skinned shrimp wontons and springy duck-egg noodles in a rich broth. Quintessential Hong Kong.
add.tips: Cash only (cards not accepted); shared tables, quick turnover, queues at peak. Hours reported as 12:00-00:30.
add.addressEn: G/F, 51 Parkes Street, Jordan, Kowloon

add.name: Cheung Hing Kee Shanghai Pan-fried Buns
add.intro: A tiny street-food shop with crispy-bottomed, soup-filled shengjian buns. Quick, cheap, and a Bib Gourmand.
add.tips: Mostly takeaway with limited counter seating; queues at peak. Payment details conflict between sources; carry some cash.
add.addressEn: Shop 6A, G/F, 48 Lock Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Chi Lin Nunnery & Nan Lian Garden
add.intro: A calm Tang-dynasty-style wooden temple complex with a classical Chinese garden of pavilions, lotus ponds and bonsai, tucked among high-rises. Both are free and feel a world away from the city.
add.tips: Go on a weekday morning for soft light and few people; keep voices down and no flash inside the temple halls. Check if the nunnery halls are open (reported 09:00-16:30) since the garden stays open later.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Island Line to Quarry Bay, change to Kwun Tong Line to Diamond Hill (Exit C2), about 35 min. Taxi about 25-30 min.
add.hours: Nan Lian Garden daily 07:00-21:00 (per Chi Lin official site via search snippet; one guide says 19:00, confirm); Chi Lin Nunnery halls commonly reported 09:00-16:30. Closed in Typhoon Signal 8.
add.addressEn: Chi Lin Nunnery, 5 Chi Lin Drive, Diamond Hill (Nan Lian Garden: 60 Fung Tak Road, opposite)
add.addressZh: 九龍鑽石山志蓮道5號(南蓮園池:鳳德道60號)

add.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
add.intro: Hong Kong's most famous working Taoist temple, with red pillars, golden roofs and clouds of incense, where locals shake fortune sticks (kau chim). Great for seeing real daily religious life.
add.tips: Go 07:30-09:00 before tour buses; photograph architecture and incense, not worshippers' faces, and no flash. Use the free-standing fortune-telling arcade for English-speaking fortune tellers if you want a reading (ask price first).
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Island Line to Quarry Bay, Kwun Tong Line to Wong Tai Sin (Exit B2), about 35 min. Taxi about 25 min.
add.hours: Daily 07:30-16:30 per official site (Wikipedia says 07:00-17:00; use official). Longer hours on 1st and 15th of lunar month.
add.addressEn: 2 Chuk Yuen Village, Wong Tai Sin, Kowloon

add.name: Kowloon Walled City Park
add.intro: A Jiangnan-style garden on the site of the notorious Kowloon Walled City, with the preserved Yamen building and a small exhibition on the city's history and its film fame.
add.tips: Dawn is quietest. The free film-set exhibition in the Yamen uses first-come tickets collected on site (opens 09:00), so go in the morning; it holds only 60 people.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Quarry Bay, Kwun Tong Line to Diamond Hill, Tuen Ma Line to Sung Wong Toi (Exit B3), then 15 min walk; about 45 min. Taxi via Cross-Harbour Tunnel about 25 min.
add.hours: Park daily 06:30-23:00; exhibition daily 09:00-19:00 (hours differ by season per secondary sources)
add.addressEn: Junction of Tung Tau Tsuen Road and Tung Ching Road, Kowloon City
add.addressZh: 九龍城東頭村道與東正道交界

add.name: 1881 Heritage
add.intro: The former Marine Police headquarters (built 1884), now a courtyard of colonnaded colonial buildings, shops and restaurants, lit warmly at night. A short walk from the Star Ferry, Clock Tower and harbour promenade.
add.tips: Come at dusk to catch the courtyard lights, then walk to the waterfront for the 8pm Symphony of Lights. The Clock Tower (1915 railway terminus remnant) is 3 min away.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Island Line to Admiralty, Tsuen Wan Line to Tsim Sha Tsui (Exit L5/E), about 20 min; or Star Ferry from Central/Wan Chai.
add.hours: Public courtyard roughly 07:00-00:00 (secondary sources; shops/restaurants vary); free guided tours by phone booking per HKTB
add.addressEn: 2A Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

add.name: Sham Shui Po (Apliu Street & Fuk Wing Street)
add.zh: 深水埗(鴨寮街及福榮街)
add.intro: Hong Kong's most local, gritty district: electronics and flea-market stalls, fabric lanes, Toy Street and humble noodle shops, including the original Tim Ho Wan at 9-11 Fuk Wing Street. Best for real everyday street life.
add.tips: Bring cash; go late afternoon for markets and food. Ask before photographing stallholders. The Michelin guide suggests Lau Sum Kee noodles on Fuk Wing Street as a first stop.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Island Line to Admiralty, Tsuen Wan Line to Sham Shui Po (Exit A2), about 30 min.
add.hours: Markets about 09:00 to late; shops vary
add.addressEn: Apliu Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon (MTR Sham Shui Po Exit A2)

add.name: Ping Shek Estate
add.area: Ngau Chi Wan / Choi Hung, Kowloon
add.intro: A 1970s public housing estate with seven blocks named after coloured stones, famous for a square courtyard shot looking straight up. It is a 10-min walk from Choi Hung Estate.
add.tips: It is a residential estate: be quiet, don't point cameras into flats, no drones or tripods in corridors. Photographers shoot the courtyard of the 'Lam Shek House' (reported by one Chinese blog) at midday.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: Quarry Bay, Kwun Tong Line to Choi Hung (Exit A1), then walk about 10 min; about 35 min.
add.hours: Open access estate, no formal hours
add.addressEn: 2 Clear Water Bay Road, Ngau Chi Wan, Kowloon
add.addressZh: 九龍牛池灣清水灣道2號坪石邨

add.name: Graham Street mural
add.intro: A famous blocky street-art mural of stacked flats, painted in 2012 and inspired by the Kowloon Walled City, on a steep market lane near Tai Kwun and PMQ.
add.tips: Expect a queue to pose on the steps; watch for passing cars and trolleys. Go early morning before crowds.
add.getting: From Causeway Bay: MTR to Central (Exit D2) then 10 min uphill walk, or taxi.
add.addressEn: Graham Street at Hollywood Road, Central (wall facing 45-53 Graham Street)
add.addressZh: 中環嘉咸街與荷李活道交界

Star Ferry.essentialWhy: The best harbour view for a few dollars.
Star Ferry.area: Central or Wan Chai ↔ Tsim Sha Tsui
Star Ferry.getting: Two piers, both going to Tsim Sha Tsui. Central Pier 7 is easiest from Booth (taxi or MTR to Central, then a 10 min walk). Wan Chai Pier is easiest from the Park Lane (about 10 min by taxi).
Star Ferry.tips: Sit on the upper deck at dusk. Go over from Central or Wan Chai, walk the Tsim Sha Tsui promenade, then ride back after dark for the lit-up skyline.
Star Ferry.addressZh: 中環天星碼頭（7號碼頭）／ 灣仔天星碼頭 ／ 尖沙咀天星碼頭

Victoria Peak & the Peak Tram.essentialTitle: See the skyline from the Peak
Victoria Peak & the Peak Tram.essentialWhy: Go at sunset and stay for the lights.
Victoria Peak & the Peak Tram.tips: Peak Tram fares are HK$82 one way and HK$116 return (2026). Buy e-tickets at thepeak.com.hk, and avoid weekend afternoons when the queue is longest. Or take the 15 bus up. For the classic skyline photo, walk 20 minutes along flat Lugard Road to the lookout.

Ding Ding tram (Kennedy Town to Shau Kei.essentialWhy: Top deck, front seat, from Kennedy Town.

Shun Kee Typhoon Shelter Seafood.essentialWhy: Garlic chilli crab on a boat.

Lan Kwai Fong (LKF).essentialTitle: A night out in LKF & Soho
